subject: Science
learningObjectives: Classify plants into herbs, shrubs, and trees
Identify parts of a plant: stem, leaf, root, flower
Understand types of roots: tap root and fibrous root
Explain leaf venation: reticulate and parallel
Describe the parts of a flower and their functions
misconceptions: Thinking that all plants with green stems are herbs (some young trees also have green stems)

practiceExercises.question: Plants with green and tender stems are called?
practiceExercises.explanation: Herbs are plants with green and tender stems. They are usually short and may not have many branches.

practiceExercises.question: Which part of the plant helps in the conduction of water?
practiceExercises.explanation: The stem conducts water from roots to leaves and other parts of the plant.

practiceExercises.question: What type of venation is seen in a peepal leaf?
practiceExercises.explanation: If the design is net-like on both sides of the midrib, the venation is reticulate.

practiceExercises.question: Which type of root system is found in grass?
practiceExercises.hint: It doesn't have a main central root.
practiceExercises.explanation: In plants like grass, all roots seem similar and these are called fibrous roots.

practiceExercises.question: The part of the flower that turns into a fruit is?
practiceExercises.hint: It is at the base of the pistil.
practiceExercises.explanation: The ovary is the lowermost and swollen part of the pistil which contains ovules and develops into a fruit.

flashcards.back: Plant with green and tender stem
Plant with branches near the base and hard stem
The design made by veins in a leaf
Loss of water in the form of vapor from leaves
The innermost part of a flower

revisionNotes: Plants are classified by size and stem type. Leaves make food (photosynthesis) and lose water (transpiration). Roots anchor and absorb.
commonMistakes: Confusing reticulate venation with tap roots

vocabulary.Photosynthesis: The process by which green plants use sunlight to make food.
vocabulary.Transpiration: The process of water movement through a plant and its evaporation from aerial parts.
vocabulary.Pollination: The transfer of pollen from anthers to the stigma of a flower.

interactiveActivities: Collect 5 different types of leaves and trace their venation in your notebook.
Soak some gram seeds and observe how the roots grow after two days.
masteryCheckpoints: Can distinguish between a shrub and a tree based on branching.
Identifies reticulate and parallel venation in leaves.
Can name the male and female parts of a flower.
introduction: Plants are all around us, from the tiny grass in your lawn to the giant banyan tree in the village. Let's dive into their world and discover how they eat, breathe, and grow!
realLifeConnection: The vegetables in your plate, the oxygen you breathe, and the beautiful flowers in the park all come from the hard work of plants.
storyBasedExplanation: Paheli and Boojho went to a garden. They noticed that while some plants stood tall, others needed support to climb. They wondered why the leaves of grass looked so different from the leaves of a rose bush.
childFriendlyExplanation: Think of a plant as a living factory. Roots gather water like straws, stems are the elevators carrying supplies, and leaves are the chefs cooking food using sunlight!
teacherExplanation: This chapter focuses on the morphological study of plants. We classify them based on their habit and study the internal and external structure of roots, stems, leaves, and flowers.
handsOnActivities: Help your child plant a seed in a transparent cup and observe the root and shoot growth.
Take a walk in a garden and try to find one herb, one shrub, and one tree.
animationScript: Scene 1: A seed sprouting underground. Roots go down, shoot goes up. Scene 2: A time-lapse of a flower opening its petals. Scene 3: Water moving up a stem like a blue light.
videoScript: Host in a botanical garden. 'Hi kids! See this hibiscus flower? If we look closely inside, we can find the yellow stamens and the central pistil. Each part has a very important job!'
parentNotes: Encourage your child to water plants and talk about how plants are living things that need care. Identify common plants in your neighborhood together.
teacherNotes: Bring real plant specimens to class. Use a magnifying glass to show ovules inside the ovary. Explain the relationship between leaf venation and root type.
learningOutcomes: Students will be able to classify plants, identify functions of various plant parts, and describe the basic reproductive parts of a flower.
